description: AFDEP extraction of the measured Apache-2.0 directional protocol, with native CUDA compilation replacing DeepEP generic runtime JIT
snapshot_note: The directional implementation was an uncommitted patch on the base commit; base commit alone does not contain this implementation.
kernel_preservation: At initial extraction: layout.hpp and kernels.cuh are byte-identical after namespace/macro rename, one copyright attribution line, explicit layout include in place of JIT-prepend comment, and diagnostic text rename. No arithmetic, synchronization, or transport instruction changed. Subsequent device changes are listed in protocol_changes; extracted_file_sha256 preserves the initial hashes and current_file_sha256 identifies the current files.
host_changes: Compile 15 existing kernel specializations into CUDA extension instead of per-kernel DeepEP JIT compilation.
Launch the same kernels in the same stream and operation order with 256 threads and zero dynamic shared memory.
Use AFDEP minimal NCCL runtime and CUDA device properties, eliminating dependency on DeepEP/vLLM/AFD-plugin/DeepGEMM.
Default to measured tuned 132 local SMs and eight transport stripes; preserve user configuration.
Add index bounds validation and initialization-failure cleanup.
Remove unused cpu_timeout_s constructor argument; GPU timeout and distributed bootstrap timeout remain explicit in their respective layers.
Validate 16-byte alignment of nonempty source activation and output pointers before vector-copy kernels, including storage-offset views.
verification: The original implementation was validated on eight H100 GPUs. This extracted build requires its own GPU validation before claiming equivalence or performance.

protocol_changes.description: Add opt-in direct delivery alongside the original hybrid protocol. Compact one request per selected worker with original-token maps, return worker partials directly to the source, and reduce there. Use FULL GIN/world addressing, per-peer readiness and reuse credits, and GPU-shared GIN contexts for concurrent peer sends. Hybrid remains the default; its allocation and protocol ordering are retained.
